results.title: Fasina’s innovations now make FUOYE staff enjoy FG’s loans for commercial farming, others-Dr. Akinsorotan, Director, CEDISS | News
results.snippet: By Wole Balogun S.A Media to VC Dr. Akinsorotan Ademola is the Acting Director, Centre for Entrepreneurship Development, Innovation and Support Services (CEDISS) of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE). In this interview, he tells the University Media Team (UMT) that the innovative ideas and leadership skills of the incumbent Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina has revived the CEDISS, making the centre more productive and effective to meeting the needs of the University community and the host communities. Besides, Dr. Akinsorotan said through the VC’s productive leadership, the centre has recently secured loans for agric business for both serving and retiring members of staff, secured land for such Enterprise among other achievements. We bring you excerpts of the interview: Dr. Akinsorotan, CEDISS’ Acting Director, FUOYE. UMT: What is the role of your centre in university education? Dr. Akinsorotan: The centre is statutorily established to ensure that students are adequately equipped for the working life after graduation. We take them in as raw materials, we process them and turn them into viable product. We achieved this laudable mandate through the vision and support of our Vice Chancellor, Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina. Our programs start from the first day with orientation for the new student till graduation. The new paradigm shift is teaching ideation and venture creation in all field and career at different faculties. Hence we have at least an Entrepreneurial officer in charge of each faculty. We aimed to produce a new breed of innovative and problem solving entrepreneurs who will transform society and revamp the national economy by being a job creators rather than job seekers. UMT: To what extent can we say CEDISS has achieved their statutory roles? It’s a journey for us. We are not there yet but we are not where we use to be. In 2022, FUOYE has 3 students in the best 10 out of 750 students from various institutions in the south west region in the 2022 Enterprise challenge competition. We eventually came first in the pitching among the best 10 finalist. There had been various other competitions that our students has participated in and excel. A lot of graduates of our institutions are CEO of companies and we are so proud of them. UMT: We leant that your centre has secured loans from the Federal Government for agriculture business for the benefit of the University community, please elaborate more on this laudable development sir. Dr. Aminsorotan: Following the Federal Government circular dated 19th April, 2022 with reference number PNA/12301/S.1458/T2/37, the Head of Service of the Federation approved the implementation of the Federal Service Entrepreneurship Programme (FPSEP) as part of measures to improve the welfare of Federal Public Servants. To this end, a development programme dubbed “Agripreneurship Scheme” was introduced by the Centre for serving staff and prospective Retirees in the University community with the aim of creating opportunities that will encourage and develop staff to be financially self-reliant and productive citizens via crop production and animal rearing. It is focused on creating a better community which centres on creating a strong and independent individual while elevates their standard of living. UMT: What are the objectives of the programme? Dr. Akinsorotan: The specific objectivies include unlocking the potential of staff members by exposing them to skill acquisition in farming and agro allied ventures as well as inculcate in them the core values of industry, commitment, innovation, passion and creativity; to instill in staff, the spirit of entrepreneurship, leadership attributes and interpersonal relationship required in setting up and engaging in enterprise creation, to empower staff with sustainable alternative source of income which will enhance their independency and productivity, to empower them to translate unmet needs in their communities into viable and sustainable income generating opportunities for themselves and others. Dr. Akinsorotan, CEDISS’ Acting Director, FUOYE. Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina, Vice-Chancellor (FUOYE) UMT: How does it run sir? Dr. Aminsorotan: The programme is premised on: access to loan facilities by financial institution (Bank of Agriculture) to prosecute the farming processes in line with their mandate to provide agricultural credit facilities to support all agricultural value chain activities, provide non-agricultural micro credit, savings mobilization and capacity development, allocation of land by the Management of our University (Federal University Oye Ekiti) at reasonable amount in Ifaki and Itaji communities where the Institution presently have hectares of land, provision of technical and professional support by our centre, the Centre for Entrepreneurship Development, Innovation and Support Services (CEDISS) i.e professional advice and guidance, visits to site, security, insurance etc Its execution follows thelis pattern, interested staff are to visit the Entrepreneurship Centre to obtain a form to indicate interest, confirm farming options and type of facility they are interested in; There will be a five (5) day seminar/workshop for all interested staff to intimate them about the program; Signing of memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Centre who stands as surety with the bank which is the facility provider; Deployment to site after training and proper documentation UMT: How will the loans be disbursed? Dr. Aminsorotan: The bursary department will deduct the loan which will be given at reducing 12% rate. What it means is that as you pay back, the 12% will be on your new balance till you finished paying the loan. Hence invariably the interest rate will eventually be around 7-8% overall. UMT: We have also leant that you have visited already established University Entrepreneur centres to u see study them and also build partnership with them in a bid to be more effective and productive in FUOYE, how has this helped you and what other projects are under way? Dr. Akinsorotan: There are big projects by staff and students that are at different stages of completion. Notable among them is the 9ce-ride project. This project was conceived by me and the main purpose is to ease the hectic transportation system on campus. We intend to control rider’s behavior and attitude to befit the culture in an academic environment; the bike is a hybrid device developed for safe and cheap transportation in FUOYE campuses for a start and later deployed to all campuses of higher institutions in Nigeria and beyond. There is no petrol, no carbon emission. The billing method is so easy. Student will buy a card specially designed for the ride and click on the ride to use it. There are other projects like: • Cordless phone charger • Laptop car charger • Wrist band GPS location monitoring device • Wrist band blood pressure monitoring device • Imagery and sounds at sharp bends on the highway to reduce accident • Smart house device that monitor your facilities from a distance • Smart greenhouse device Just to mention a few. A lot of SMEs created by students that are doing well under our tutelage from the Centre. We started a farm shortly after a program for the would-be retirees in the university. We presently have over 200 stands of plantain growing, 600 stand of an hybrid tomatoes and other vegetables. We have 5 fish ponds revived and ready for stocking. If you are a staff of FUOYE and you have about 2 to 3 years to retire, you will be trained by our centre before your disengagement. This will give you a strong footing at retirement. Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina has revolutionized the centre completely and has given us a new direction for effective training and remolding the students for critical thinking in other to generate innovative ideas in their different carrier. He has helped us to also impacted members of staff through different programs. The ‘Town n Gown’ initiative has been supported adequately by the Vice Chancellor. FUOYE CEDISS will be an incubation hub that will generate ideas for economic stability of this nation. Jobs will be created, machines and devices will be developed for various use by people and solutions to mankind will evolved by the centre.

results.title: Convocation: Fasina has brought development to communities, jobs, admission opportunities, -Dr. Adeleke, Director of Centre for Continuing Education | News
results.snippet: …as FUOYE announces new admission opportunities By Wole Balogun S.A Media to VC Dr. Omolade Adeleke is new Director of the Centre for Continuing Education of the upwardly mobile Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE). The centre manages FUOYE’s Institute of Part Time Studies (IPTS) and Distance Learning (D.L). Through the centre, FUOYE has greatly fulfilled one of its core mandates as a federal educational institution, community services, by having its presence in five adjourning communities along the Oye-Ikole axis. The communities in chronological order are Ifaki-Ekiti, Ayegbaji-Ekiti, Ire-Ekiti, Ikole-Ekiti and Ayedun-Ekiti. Dr. Omolade Adeleke Director of the Centre for Continuing Education Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina VICE CHANCELLOR FUOYE According to Dr. Adeleke, meaningful development, numerous job opportunities and admission opportunities have been created by the Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina’s administration with the Centre for Continuing education through its IPTS. In this chat with Wole Balogun of the University Media Team (UMT) the Director of FUOYE’s Centre for Continuing Education, revealed other laudable achievements of the Vice-Chancellor in two years of his five-year tenure as the institution prepares for its 7th Convocation ceremony which kicks off February 6. Excerpts: UMT: By February 11, 2023, it will be two years that Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina assumed office as the fourth substantive Vice-Chancellor of FUOYE, what is your impression about his performance so far? Dr. Adeleke: The administration of Prof. Abayomi Sunday Fasina started on a good note and one of the vibrant achievements the Fasina administration has made is to kick start the lnstitite of Part Time Studies (IPTS) immediately he came on board in 2021. The institute has been his brain child and he shared his visions on it, so the successes witnessed today in the institute is a product of a well-thought-out mission and when you have a visionary leader like Prof. Abayomi Fasina, you would always want to do more. And we are ready to replicate the same success in the new mission, the Centre for Continuing Education for which l have been appointed as the pioneer Director. UMT: So, what has been the achievements recorded in IPTS which you are planning to replicate in the new Centre? Dr. Adeleke: Thanks to our amiable VC who deemed it fit that with our impressive performance in IPTS, we should be able to replicate same in the centre which we are pioneering and this centre now, we will be managing both the Distance Learning lnstitute and the lnstitute of Part Time studies. I am most grateful to the VC for this appointment. One of the hallmarks of the VC is his love for the communities in Ekiti, especially those adjourning towns to Oye-Ekiti where the University’s main campus is located. He has passion for developing people and communities and derives joy in building people and careers, and expanding the scope of development behind Oye-Ekiti. That has been his watchword and that is why you can see the institute of part time studies moving from one town to another. Currently, we are in five towns, we have part of our faculty of agriculture namely departments of Food Science & Technology and Plant ad Animal Production in Ayedun-Ekiti, the rest of the faculty of agriculture and the Tourism and hotel management that has just been approved are all in Ikole campus. Ire-Ekiti has Computer Science , Mass Communication and Library and Information Science . While Ayegbaju is the home of all faculties of Social Sciences, Management Studies and Arts. Ayegbaju is the headquarters of our institute of part time studies. The fifth campus is springing up now in Ifaki as work is currently on going there. That is where we are having the post graduate arm of the institute of part time studies, where we shall be having MBA, Masters in public administration, Accounting and others which we are already admitting students for. Now what is the motive behind planting of all these campuses? One, Prof. Abayomi Fasina deemed it fit not only to impact on Oye-Ekiti but also the adjourning towns , l have said that before, two, he believes that since government cannot do this alone, we should find a means of bringing in the communities to participate in the development of our education sector. Three, the VC believes that bringing in towns will further create job opportunities for people around these areas. Four, the initiative will provide additional admission opportunities for students . For your information, we have over 50,000 applicants for the last jamb who applied for FUOYE alone. Those applicants picked FUOYE as their first choice and as you know, the qouta of the University is less than 8,000. So, that means over 40,000 prospective students will be roaming about looking for admissions and waiting for another jamb. And that is the idea behind part time, as we are spreading, there are opportunities for us to accommodate prospective students that are unable to secure admissions through Jamb. So, with these four points, you would see that the idea behind part time institute is well thought of. UMT: How have the host communities embraced this gesture of community services by the Prof. Fasina led administration sir? Dr. Adeleke: Let me tell you what we have achieved in this effort with the support from Prof. Fasina. One, let me start with Ire-Ekiti, it was a town that wasn’t noticed before as there was no robust social activities that can put the town on the global map in terms of education, but now if you enter the town, the first sign board you will see is that of our institute of part time studies, and the cooperation of the community has been enormous. They erected buildings for our campus there, and furnished it themselves. They even bought the power generating set for us in the campus. Of recent, one of the illustrious sons of the town, Aare Akomolafe Adebayo, came into the limelight and after a few discussions with the institute of part time studies, he pledged his commitment to the cause of the part time programmes, and l want to tell you that today, the man has made tremendous contribution to the development of the institute, first, he donated an 18-Seater bus which is well over N10 million, two, he donated another N5 million to equip our computer laboratory. We want Computer Science to start and be domiciled in Ire-Ekiti and now we have over 50 Computer systems to have a befitting computer laboratory in Ire-Ekiti. 18 seater bus well above 10 milon, 50 computers . And again, as if that was not enough, this man has plegded to build a standard CBT centre for us in the Ire-Ekiti campus. and that CBT centre is worth over N60 million. It is a jamb CBT centre where we would have about 300 computer systems in it and it will be with all network accessories provided and then server will be built from the scratch. Then again, another illustrious son of that town has given us a whole building which he was using as public library before, that is Chief Femi Ajayi . There is a public library in Ire-Ekiti called Juliana Ajayi public library, it has now been gifted to the FUOYE institute of part time studies. And all documents have been handed over to us. We have renovated the building to house the computer laboratory for now. Ire-Ekiti has been so cooperating and if you go to the town now, there is a beehive of activities . Students of Mass Communication are there, so also students of Library and Information Science are there and in the next few months, they will be receiving students of Computer Science there also. We bless God for their cooperation. For Ikole-Ekiti, they have been phenomenal. I want to tell you that the Ikole Development Union has single-handedly built a campus for us. When l say a campus, l mean what you can call an ideal mini-campus has been built for us by the Ikole Development Union, and it is powered by Barrister Kayode Filani. He single-handedly built the campus in the name of the community’s union. He is a native and illustrious son of Ikole-Ekiti. Currently, we have about six buildings built from the scratch by him on about 20 plots of land, which he has donated to the institute of part time studies. Currently, we have about four classrooms there, each with 300 seats for students. The buildings are well furnished, painted and powered. There are also boreholes dug to bring adequate supply of water. And we have two buildings under construction there. The adjourning roads to that campus have been cleared so that they can be motorable and the place can be assessible. Hall 1 Hall 2 Computer Lab Now, we have our mini campus for the institute over there. The VC will be commissioning all these projects during the coming Convocation ceremony. The VC will also be supervising the foundation laying ceremony of the CBT centre being built for us by Aare Akomolafe in Ire-Ekiti, so also will he commission the new bus donated to us . So, we have an array of achievements and these are just to say a few. In Ayedun- Ekiti, in their little way, they have contributed to the growth of our campus in their community. So, as we bless God, all these great achievements were possible because of the encouragement given to us by the VC to the leadership of part time studies to engage the communities where our presence have been established in developing the education sector . And in the long run, the glory is coming back to the towns as their commercial activities and economic development are improving. Now, all these acheivements are products of hard work, steadfastness and idea generations and discussions. We thank God for the encouragement from our Vice-Chancellor and we are ready to bring to bear the same energy to build the Centre for Continuing education, particularly the Distance Learning institute that we are starting already. We will take the centre to greater heights. It shall become one of the centres of excellence in Nigeria. We want to really appreciate our Vice-Chancellor for his immense support given to the leadership.

results.title: Pomp as FUOYE Director becomes Associate Professor of Economics | News
results.snippet: By Wole Balogun S. A. media to VC It was pomp on Wednesday as the Governing Council of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) approved the appointment of the Director of the Centre for Continuing Education, Dr. Omolade Adeleke, to the professorial cadre. Dr. Omolade Adeleke Dr Adeleke was appointed as Associate Professor by the Appointments and Promotion Committee A&PC of the University on Monday, March 13, 2023, after due procedure was followed according to the Regulations of the Ivory Tower. The newly minted Associate Professor of Economics has won the NRF sponsorship research grant in South Africa twice. He also clinched the TETFUND research grants in FUOYE in the year 2018. Dr. Adeleke had his first and second Degrees in Economics from Ekiti State University (EKSU). He bagged his and PhD in Economics from the University of KwaZulu Natal in South Africa . He was appointed Deputy Director, lnstitute of Part Time Studies (IPTS) in 2021 and after serving for about two years as the director of IPTS and considering his numerous achievements within the two years in charge of IPTS which has ensured that both assets and revenue of the University improved tremendously, the management elevated him the Director of the Institute and in 2023 elevated further to the post of the Director, Centre for Continuing Education (CCE) of FUOYE. He has both the institutes of part time studies and Distant Learning under his purview as the Director of CCE. Dr.Adeleke has over 40 publications in accredited journals with 20 in scopus and Ibss indexed . He is a Research fellow to the University of KwaZulu Natal South Africa and has successfully produced three PhD graduates. He is also an External Examiner to the University of Cape Town, University of Johannesburg and University of KwaZulu Natal all in South Africa. The Associate Professor of Economics has attended academic conferences across the globe and such included the US, UK, Netherlands, South Africa among others As part of his academic and administrative laurels, Dr. Adeleke won the best Director in the entire University for two consecutive years of 2021 and 2022. He also emerged the students’ lecturer of the year at both Faculty and Departmental levels of the 2018/2019 academic session.

results.title: Infrastructural Development: VC hails FUOYE’s Continuing Education Centre’s Director on construction of ultra-modern admin building. | News
results.snippet: By Wole Balogun S.A Media to VC Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE), Prof. Sunday Abayomi Fasina, has on Thursday commended the Director of the Centre for Continuing Education of the University, Associate Professor Omolade Adeleke for realizing the laudable goal of building an ultra-modern administrative block for the use of the Centre with collaborative efforts with the students union and without getting any financial commitment from the University management. The new administrative building of the Centre houses the offices of its administrative officers and the Director. It was built with resources by the Centre as supported financially by the Centre’s students’ Union body. The edifice was commissioned by the VC and his management team on Thursday, August 10, 2023 at the Ayegbaju satellite campus of the institution. Christened after the Vice-Chancellor, the administrative block boasts of high quality building materials that assured that it would be an enduring facility for the use of the Centre. While commissioning the Prof. Abayomi Fasina ultramodern administrative block at the Ayegbaju campus on Thursday, the excited VC eulogized Dr. Adeleke saying that he has always been passionate about bringing about meaningful growth and development to the University. He described him as an excellent go-getter who brings great ideas into fruition against all odds and promised to always support his visions. The VC said: “This is awesome and l am very proud of Dr. Omolade Adeleke. If we have just five of him in this University, we would be far greater than how we are now. You have really made us proud as our Director. And l will continue to do everything humanly possible to support you. You have made me to have so much confidence in you, as you have shown to us that things are doable. Many people come to my office to give excuses on why one or two things are not possible, but you have always come to me to encourage me and prove to me that things are doable. You have so much energy and are willing to make things much better . I appreciate you a lot,” he said. Prof. Fasina also used the happy moment to advise other appointees of the University to emulate the exemplary leadership being provided by Dr. Adeleke in managing the the University’s Centre for Continuing Education and achieving so much.
